title: Cockroach Janta Party holds Lehra Do Tiranga protest at Azad Maidan
seoTitle: Mumbai CJP Lehra Do Tiranga protest

tea.why: Protesters oppose the arrest of party leaders in New Delhi, the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, and current election processes.
tea.want: Resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner, release of detained activists, and a return to paper ballots for future elections.
tea.changed: Oct 16: The protest concluded peacefully at Azad Maidan after receiving official permission from the Mumbai Police.

summary: On October 16, 2026, the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) held a 'Lehra Do Tiranga' demonstration at Azad Maidan in Mumbai. Organised in solidarity with protesters in New Delhi, the event featured speeches from party volunteers and visiting activists, including MNS leader Sandeep Deshpande and social activist Anjali Damania. Participants demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, the withdrawal of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, and the release of party leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, who were reportedly detained in Delhi. Protesters also called for the replacement of Electronic Voting Machines with ballot papers. Unlike in Delhi, Mumbai authorities granted permission for the gathering, which concluded peacefully in the afternoon. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis stated that regime changes must occur through elections rather than street protests.
demands: Resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar
Withdrawal of Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls
Introduction of ballot papers for future elections
response: Mumbai Police granted permission for the one-day protest at Azad Maidan. Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis stated that regime changes should be decided in Parliament and through elections, rather than on the streets.

crowd.text: The Free Press Journal estimated 50 to 100 attendees, while The Economic Times reported around 50 supporters.

updates.text: CJP supporters gathered at Azad Maidan in Mumbai for the 'Lehra Do Tiranga' protest.
The protest concluded peacefully in the afternoon following speeches from political and social activists.
